attributes.residual: REGISTER_ONLY and now PURE: STRUCTURAL = 0 (the register-normalised scan reports zero words unexplainable by renaming, and the stack-slot census is identical slot-for-slot on both sides). What remains is 121 paired words of callee-saved RECOLOURING plus 4 unpaired words that are one `addi r3,r1,52` displaced by a single slot at two sites (schedule-class, permutation-eligible). NOT webfrank-eligible: the recolour is not CONSISTENT. Two bijection breaks remain, and they are the whole task: r20 is claimed by both target r19 (13 words) and target r31 (2 words), and f30 is claimed by both target f29 (3 words) and target f31 (11 words). THE COMPLETE 23-WEB COLOUR TABLE, keyed by def offset, target -> ours (this is the actionable form - a per-register majority tally is not): 0x030 playerIdx r21->r22; 0x034 mode r25->r23; 0x038 ctx r28->r29; 0x03c spread r29->r30; 0x040 partner r23->r26; 0x044 found r22->r25; 0x058 p r24->r24; 0x094 r30->r31; 0x0bc i@block1 r26->r27; 0x124 other@block1 r19->r20; 0x274 gPlayers base r31->r20 (GROUP A); 0x278 j r25->r23; 0x280 modulo r27->r28; 0x29c other@loop2 r26->r27; 0x364 k r19->r19; 0x368 8-step induction r20->r21; 0x468 other@fallback r20->r20; 0x5a4 &gDefaultPlayerPosition[2] r23->r25 (GROUP B, wants r26); 0x5b0 &gDefaultPlayerPosition[1] r22->r23 (GROUP B, wants r25); 0x5e4 &gFloorCollisionResult+0x44 r25->r20 (GROUP B, wants r23); 0x63c &gDefaultPlayerPosition[0] r20->r21; 0x640 i@final r26->r26; 0x644 8-step induction r21->r22. FPR: 0x1c8 f28->f28; 0x1d4+0x1fc sin/cos fmr f29->f30; 0x270 thresh(first) f29->f30; 0x638 thresh(reload) f29->f29; 0x1b0 sx f30->f29; 0x39c+0x3a0 r f30->f31; 0x5a8+0x5bc r f30->f31; 0x1b4 sz f31->f31; 0x5c8 halfR f31->f30. THE ROOT IS ONE PACKING DECISION, NOT 12 INDEPENDENT WORDS: the two builds have IDENTICAL instruction streams, identical def sites and therefore identical interference graphs, so the allocator's WEB VISIT ORDER is what differs. Target packs other@block1 with k into r19; ours gives k r19 alone and pushes other@block1 into r20, which then carries FOUR webs (other@block1, other@fallback, gFloorCollisionResult, gPlayers) against the target's busiest three, and every later assignment shifts one slot along the preference sequence r19,r20,r21,r22,r25,r23,r26,r27,r28,r29,r30,r31. Group B is a CONSEQUENCE of that packing, not an independently steerable target: the three pointer webs simply inherit whichever callee-saved register died last, and probes 5-7 confirm the source cannot reorder that. DO NOT RETRY axes 1, 5, 6, 7, nor v2's s/c value-identity split or outer-pad splits. The untried directions worth a future pass are the address-web forms themselves (a named pointer local for gFloorCollisionResult+0x44, accepting the base+displacement change it will cause at the first use) and `register` storage class on other/p.
